2608.25841.title: VINCENT: Validated Interaction Network for Cross-drug Explanation of Therapeutics
2608.25841.paper_summary: Drug synergy prediction estimates whether two drugs produce a stronger joint effect than expected from their individual activities. For drug combination discovery, a single synergy score is often not enough: researchers also need to know which molecular regions jointly drive the prediction. We study motif-pair synergy explanation, which identifies pairs of chemically coherent regions, one from each drug, that jointly contribute to predicted synergy. Existing interpretable synergy models expose atom- or substructure-level signals, but their explanations are built into the predictor architecture, and none validates cross-drug region scores under repeated perturbations or feeds that evidence back to refine the explanation. A reliable motif-pair explanation should instead be chemically coherent, perturbation-stable, and aligned with predictor behavior. We introduce VINCENT (Validated Interaction Network for Cross-drug Explanation of Therapeutics), a post-training framework for a fixed interaction-aware synergy predictor. VINCENT extracts atom-pair evidence from attention and gradient signals, groups atoms into chemically coherent motifs, and validates candidate motif pairs through repeated local perturbations. The validated evidence is fed back to refine motif assignments, yielding explanations that satisfy these three criteria. On a 25-pair literature-annotated subset, VINCENT achieves a mean motif recall of 0.826 (95% CI: 0.78-0.87), compared with 0.49-0.66 for baselines. Across all 71 test pairs, its validated interaction scores yield a TP/TN separation of 3.36. These results show that closed-loop perturbation validation recovers literature-supported molecular regions more accurately than existing alternatives while producing cross-drug interaction scores that better reflect predictor behavior.
2608.25841.paper_summary_zh: 藥物協同作用預測估計兩種藥物是否產生比其各自活性預期更強的聯合效果。對於藥物組合的發現，單一的協同作用分數往往不夠：研究人員還需要知道哪些分子區域共同驅動預測。我們研究動機對偶協同作用解釋，該解釋識別來自每種藥物的化學一致區域對，這些區域共同促成預測的協同作用。現有的可解釋協同作用模型揭示原子或子結構層級的信號，但它們的解釋內建於預測器架構中，且沒有一個在重複擾動下驗證交叉藥物區域分數或將該證據反饋以完善解釋。可靠的動機對偶解釋應該是化學一致的、擾動穩定的，並且與預測器行為對齊。我們引入 VINCENT（交叉藥物治療解釋的經過驗證的互動網絡），這是一個針對固定互動意識協同作用預測器的後訓練框架。VINCENT 從注意力和梯度信號中提取原子對證據，將原子分組為化學一致的動機，並通過重複的局部擾動來驗證候選動機對。經過驗證的證據被反饋以完善動機分配，產生滿足這三個標準的解釋。在一個包含 25 對文獻註釋子集的測試中，VINCENT 的平均動機召回率為 0.826（95% CI：0.78-0.87），而基準為 0.49-0.66。在所有 71 個測試對中，其經過驗證的互動分數產生了 3.36 的 TP/TN 分離。這些結果顯示，閉環擾動驗證比現有替代方案更準確地恢復文獻支持的分子區域，同時產生更能反映預測器行為的交叉藥物互動分數。
